body:
[aida:reviewer] Correction to the round you described: the head is no longer 15d1668f5d.
A fourth commit landed at 00:30 and it is NOT a test helper.

    17e27888ce  test(forge): enforce live GitLab lifecycle assertions   (the head I refused)
    09364e13dd  docs(forge): document fail-loud GitLab credentials
    15d1668f5d  test(forge): tolerate asynchronous GitLab project creation
    af2a4a6d3a  fix(forge): keep GitLab CI polling on driven root       <- NEW, aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs

WHAT THE NEW COMMIT DOES. Inside wait_for_ci_terminal's poll loop it replaces the
cwd-derived probe with the caller-injected one:

    -  let probe = ci_probe_via_forge(branch);
    +  let forge_kind = crate::forge::resolve_forge_kind(git_root);
    +  let probe = ci_probe_with_forge(git_root, forge_kind, branch);

The defect claim is REAL and I verified the mechanism rather than the comment.
ci_probe_via_forge -> probe_ci_state_for_branch, which begins with
find_project_root() (lib.rs:34361) -- process cwd, not the driven worktree. So a
GitLab wait driven from a worktree that is not the agent's cwd could resolve GitHub.
git_root is already in scope at 34526 and ci_probe_with_forge pre-exists (BUG-1037),
so the fix is minimal and correct at that one site.

WHERE IT IS A HALF-FIX. ci_probe_via_forge has FOUR remaining call sites at this head,
and in THREE of them the project root is already in scope on the adjacent lines:

  1. lib.rs:34815 -- fn watch_ci_terminal(project_root: Option<&Path>, branch: &str).
     This is the sharpest one. The SAME function passes project_root to
     wait_for_ci_terminal on the degrade path at 34801, then discards it fourteen
     lines later at 34815 on the success path. The commit fixed the callee and left
     its own caller's sibling branch. --watch-ci is therefore only half-fixed: when
     `gh run watch` succeeds, the Green/Red classification still goes through cwd.
  2. lib.rs:46027 -- project_root used at 46022 and 46024, immediately above.
  3. lib.rs:77780 -- project_root used at 77766, 77769 and 77775.

The fourth (35728, session_end) I have not established has a root in scope and I am
not claiming it.

MY POSITION. This does not change the verdict outcome -- F1 is still the open one and
nothing here touches it. TASK-1273 is a nightly-GitLab-test spec, so an incidental
production fix in the CI-wait path is arguably outside its scope entirely; that is the
part I think is yours to rule on, not mine. What is mine: if a fix ships under a
"keep polling on the driven root" subject while three same-shape sites with the root
in scope keep polling on cwd, the class gets called done. I will record these three as
an enumerated finding on the refusal unless you tell me the scope call goes the other
way and they belong somewhere else.

CI RIGHT NOW: Build (ubuntu-latest) pending at 0s on the new head, macos/windows also
pending (informational per your note), merge-hold-gate failing as the hold, and
"GitLab live forge smoke" reports SKIPPING on this PR run -- which is itself the
reason F1 cannot close from a PR run.
subject: PR-1978 head moved AGAIN to af2a4a6d - round is now FOUR commits and the 4th is production code, half-fixed (3 sibling call sites)
